scope: Read-only comparative terrain for shared radar presentation. No product scoring, privacy policy, API or implementation is decided.

grounding.claim: Shared controls use a common theme contract and native/web owned components; feature packages own domain and fetching.
Chart port is listed as next; do not assume an existing owned radar contract.

Existing radarLayout takes any node metadata attributes, normalizes by assumption, and substitutes sample attributes when absent; it cannot safely represent unknown or different per-axis scales as-is.

Graphics root barrel includes charts, components and hooks as well as layouts, so its root is not empirically a platform-neutral-only import. The explicit layouts subpath exists, but its dependency boundary must be verified before use by kit code.
Legacy flat component imports frozen primitives and Theme, and onChange is not called. Wrapping it would carry a prohibited new legacy import and cannot deliver editing.
Existing renderer draws fixed outer-radius vertices rather than value-scaled geometry; reuse without correction misrepresents values.
Knowledge graph metadata attributes are Record<string, number>; that shape has no subject, perspective or per-measure version and cannot represent radar domain identity by itself.

options.description: Upstream owning domains supply already-authorized, attributed measure sets. A bounded pure projection at a verified graphics/layout seam converts explicit valid ranges and values into geometry. An owned shared-contract radar presentation renders independently in native and web; a feature composition supplies status and attribution.
advantages: One geometry contract can be verified independently from platform rendering.
Native/web owned kit names and shared props follow the current architecture.
Feature remains responsible for subject identity, values, permissions and data loading.
costs: Existing radarLayout must not be called unchanged: fallback samples, any input and implicit 0-1 range are incompatible with unknown and per-axis range.
Graphics package root exports native and data-bearing modules; package dependency and subpath platform neutrality must be checked, not assumed.
An owned chart contract and renderer require both-platform tests, world recipes and gallery evidence before promotion.
options.status: candidate, subject to package boundary check and product review

options.description: Compose an accessible per-dimension list/table using existing owned Surface, Text and controls within the owning feature or browser app, with optional chart geometry later behind an owned chart port. Keep each measure set separate and use domain adapters only after owner decisions.
advantages: Smallest truthful initial display without a new cross-package graph or legacy renderer.
Lists can distinguish unknown, units, ranges and attribution without forcing polygon interpolation.
Uses existing kit parts and does not require a dependency upgrade.
costs: Does not provide the requested polygon until an owned chart is added; it is a staged presentation option, not full visual equivalence.
Native and web feature compositions still need shared semantic contract and parity checks.
Do not build a reusable chart ad hoc inside one app; promote common rendering to the kit when required.
options.status: candidate for a safe first slice; not a substitute for an authorized full radar

comparisonBoundary.inputSketch: One explicitly identified subject plus independently attributed measure-set(s): perspective, owner/source and version, axis IDs, labels, units, declared ranges and value | unknown. This is a proposal for presentation, not an existing domain API.
rules: Keep unknown distinct from numeric zero; never impute sample attributes or connect missing vertices as measured zero.

Match comparisons only when subject identity, measure IDs, versions, units, axis definitions and ranges are compatible; otherwise show separate sets or a clear unavailable comparison. Whether different observers or perspectives can be compared is an owner decision, not a chart inference.
Reject non-finite values, invalid or zero-width ranges and out-of-range input at a documented boundary; do not silently clamp or invent a score.
Preserve provenance and observer attribution; do not conflate self-report with another person's observation or treat selected context as permission.

Represent loading, empty, access denied and unavailable separately. Provide an accessible text/table equivalent with each value, unit and unknown; include non-gesture edit alternatives only after editing authority exists.
Honor reduced motion and preserve information when animation is disabled or interrupted; do not imply change over time without versioned evidence.

recommendation: For an approved shared chart, option 1 fits the kit's planned chart-port direction if the graphics subpath boundary is proven and a typed non-fabricating geometry function is introduced. Option 2 is a lower-risk textual first increment when chart design or ownership is unresolved. Neither option authorizes current product integration or selection of measures.
checks: Verify UI kit contracts, world recipes, both barrels, native/web unit tests, UI boundary and world gates; visual and assistive-technology behavior needs actual browser/device evidence.
Test permutations, missing values, distinct subject/measure/version, heterogeneous ranges, invalid inputs and accessible equivalent; include failure/denied states without treating them as zero.
No dependency API or upgrade is recommended here; no installed SVG declaration or live upstream search was used for a specific API claim.
limits: No production code edited; no external source research or live UI execution performed.
This bounded code survey does not establish product authority, installed backend capabilities, safe disclosure or complete caller coverage.
Parallel architect panel was not run because parent prohibited child agents; options are a single reviewer's synthesis.
